components.note: 饣 (food, simplified 食) — meals and eating: 饿 hungry, 饱 full, 饺 dumpling; 饭 is cooked rice or a meal.
反 (fǎn) is a near sound match for fàn; also in 板 bǎn.
广 (building, shelter) — houses and shops: 床, 库, 座; 店 is a shop.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound hint; same part in 站 zhàn and 战 zhàn.

example.hanzi: 我们在那家饭店预订了一张桌子。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài nà jiā fàndiàn yùdìngle yī zhāng zhuōzi.
example.english: We reserved a table at that restaurant.
example.fact: Sobrino de Botín in Madrid, which opened in 1725, holds the Guinness World Record for the oldest restaurant in continuous operation — it's even mentioned by name in Ernest Hemingway's novel The Sun Also Rises.

examples.hanzi: 这家饭店的菜很好吃。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā fàndiàn de cài hěn hǎochī.
examples.english: The food at this restaurant is delicious.

examples.hanzi: 我们住的饭店离机场很近。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhù de fàndiàn lí jīchǎng hěn jìn.
examples.english: The hotel we are staying at is very close to the airport.

meanings: to do sth of one's own accord
opposite: passive 被動|被动[bei4 dong4]

components.note: 主 (master, host) — a lamp with a flame on top; a lamp stand was the centre of the room. 主 also sounds out 注 zhù, 住 zhù and 柱 zhù.
力 (strength) — effort and motion, as in 办, 助, 努. The part 云 stands in for 重 in the traditional 動, which was the sound clue.

example.hanzi: 她主动帮同事解决了问题。
example.pinyin: Tā zhǔdòng bāng tóngshì jiějuéle wèntí.
example.english: She took the initiative to help her colleague solve the problem.
example.fact: Organizational psychology research consistently links proactive, initiative-taking behavior at work with faster promotions and higher job satisfaction, in part because acting before being asked signals competence to supervisors more clearly than simply completing assigned tasks.

examples.hanzi: 他看到老人上车，主动让了座。
examples.pinyin: Tā kàn dào lǎorén shàng chē, zhǔdòng ràng le zuò.
examples.english: Seeing the old man board, he offered his seat on his own.

examples.hanzi: 你应该主动跟老师联系。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi zhǔdòng gēn lǎoshī liánxì.
examples.english: You should take the initiative to contact the teacher.

components.note: 易 (yì) is a loose sound clue for 踢 tī, 赐 cì and 惕 tì; the meaning "easy" comes from "change" and its early lizard picture is unproven.

example.hanzi: 这个问题不容易回答。
example.pinyin: Zhège wèntí bù róngyì huídá.
example.english: This question is not easy to answer.
example.fact: 易 has two main senses: 'easy' (容易) and 'to change or exchange' (交易 trade, 易经 the Book of Changes). In 容易 the second syllable is neutral in tone.

examples.hanzi: 这个国家的贸易很发达。
examples.pinyin: Zhège guójiā de màoyì hěn fādá.
examples.english: This country's trade is very developed.

examples.hanzi: 这种水果不易保存。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng shuǐguǒ bú yì bǎocún.
examples.english: This fruit isn't easy to store.

components.note: 平 (píng, flat) also lends its sound to 评 píng, 苹 píng and 坪 píng.
日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.hanzi: 平时他六点就起床了。
example.pinyin: Píngshí tā liù diǎn jiù qǐchuáng le.
example.english: Ordinarily, he gets up at six o'clock.
example.fact: The human body's internal clock, run by a cluster of neurons called the suprachiasmatic nucleus, naturally cycles on a period of about 24.2 hours — slightly longer than a solar day — which is why daily exposure to light is needed to keep it in sync with the outside world.

examples.hanzi: 我平时喜欢在家看书。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ píngshí xǐhuan zài jiā kànshū.
examples.english: I usually like to read at home.

examples.hanzi: 他平时不爱说话，今天却说了很多。
examples.pinyin: Tā píngshí bú ài shuōhuà, jīntiān què shuō le hěn duō.
examples.english: He usually doesn't talk much, but today he said a lot.

components.note: 钅 (metal; traditional 金) — marks metals, as in 钱 money, 铁 iron, 铜 copper; 钉 is a metal nail.
丁 (dīng) — same sound: 钉 dīng. 丁 also sounds out 盯 dīng and 订 dìng.

example.hanzi: 墙上钉着一颗钉子。
example.pinyin: Qiáng shàng dìng zhe yì kē dīngzi.
example.english: There is a nail hammered into the wall.
example.fact: 钉 is a noun 'nail' read dīng, and a verb 'to nail' read dìng, as in 钉钉子. So the sentence 钉钉子 contains both: dìng dīngzi.

examples.hanzi: 他的鞋底扎了一颗钉子。
examples.pinyin: Tā de xiédǐ zhā le yì kē dīngzi.
examples.english: A nail went into the sole of his shoe.

examples.hanzi: 我们需要买一盒钉子。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào mǎi yì hé dīngzi.
examples.english: We need to buy a box of nails.

components.note: 寸 (hand, inch) — hands and measuring, as in 寻 seek, 导 lead, 射 shoot; 对 faces someone or matches a pair. 又 here only stands in for the left side of 對.
面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.

example.hanzi: 银行就在超市的对面。
example.pinyin: Yínháng jiù zài chāoshì de duìmiàn.
example.english: The bank is right across from the supermarket.
example.fact: The Italian city of Bologna has around 38 kilometers of covered porticoes lining the streets facing each other, a network so extensive and historically significant that UNESCO added it to the World Heritage List in 2021.

examples.hanzi: 我家对面新开了一家面包店。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā duìmiàn xīn kāi le yì jiā miànbāodiàn.
examples.english: A new bakery opened across from my house.

examples.hanzi: 坐在我对面的那个人是谁？
examples.pinyin: Zuò zài wǒ duìmiàn de nàge rén shì shéi?
examples.english: Who is the person sitting across from me?

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — marks walls and confinement, as in 国, 园, 困, 围; 囚 is a person 人 inside: a prisoner.
犭 (beast, form of 犬 dog) — animals: 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狼 wolf; 犯 is to attack or violate, hence offend.

example.hanzi: 那名囚犯已经服刑十年了。
example.pinyin: Nà míng qiúfàn yǐjīng fúxíng shí nián le.
example.english: That prisoner has already served ten years.
example.fact: Alcatraz federal prison operated for 29 years and, despite its reputation as escape-proof, recorded at least 14 separate escape attempts involving 36 inmates. Officially none succeeded, though the fate of three men from the famous 1962 escape was never conclusively determined.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影讲了一个囚犯越狱的故事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎng le yí ge qiúfàn yuèyù de gùshi.
examples.english: This movie tells the story of a prisoner escaping from prison.

examples.hanzi: 囚犯在监狱里学习做木工。
examples.pinyin: Qiúfàn zài jiānyù lǐ xuéxí zuò mùgōng.
examples.english: The prisoner learns carpentry in prison.

components.note: 马 (horse) — 马 is the horse radical, as in 骑 ride, 驾; 骗 first meant to jump on a horse.
扁 (biǎn) — near sound — 骗 is piàn; 扁 also sounds out 偏 piān, 篇 piān and 遍 biàn.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 他说的话都是骗人的。
example.pinyin: Tā shuō dehuà dōu shì piànrén de.
example.english: Everything he said was a lie.
example.fact: A large meta-analysis of deception research found that people can spot lies from behavior alone with only about 54% accuracy — barely better than a coin flip — because there is no single reliable physical 'tell' that reveals lying.

examples.hanzi: 你别骗人，我才不信。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié piànrén, wǒ cái bú xìn.
examples.english: Don't lie to people; I won't believe it.

examples.hanzi: 他从来不骗人。
examples.pinyin: Tā cónglái bú piàn rén.
examples.english: He never cheats anyone.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — hearing and joining, as in 听, 聪, 闻: 联 first meant ears joined, so to link. The part 关 stands in for the traditional shape.
合 (join) — a lid fitting over an opening 口: things that fit together. 合 also appears in 答 dá, 给 gěi and 拾 shí.

example.hanzi: 两家公司决定联合开发新产品。
example.pinyin: Liǎng jiā gōngsī juédìng liánhé kāifā xīn chǎnpǐn.
example.english: The two companies decided to jointly develop a new product.
example.fact: The United Nations was founded in 1945 by 51 countries and now counts 193 member states, making it the largest intergovernmental organization on Earth, even though most of its General Assembly resolutions are non-binding.

examples.hanzi: 几家公司联合起来办了一次展览。
examples.pinyin: Jǐ jiā gōngsī liánhé qǐlai bàn le yí cì zhǎnlǎn.
examples.english: Several companies joined together to hold an exhibition.

examples.hanzi: 联合国总部在纽约。
examples.pinyin: Liánhéguó zǒngbù zài Niǔyuē.
examples.english: The United Nations headquarters is in New York.

components.note: 且 (moreover) — an old picture of an offering stand or ancestral tablet. As a sound clue it gives 祖 zǔ, 组 zǔ, 租 zū and 助 zhù.

example.hanzi: 这个房间大而且干净。
example.pinyin: Zhège fángjiān dà érqiě gānjìng.
example.english: This room is big and also clean.
example.fact: Alone 且 is literary, but it is common in 而且 ('moreover', as in 不但……而且……), 并且 and 况且. It can mean 'for the time being' in expressions like 暂且 and 姑且.

examples.hanzi: 这个办法简单而且有效。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bànfǎ jiǎndān érqiě yǒuxiào.
examples.english: This method is simple and also effective.

examples.hanzi: 这件事暂且不提。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì zànqiě bù tí.
examples.english: Let's leave this matter aside for now.

components.note: 角 (horn, corner) — a picture of an animal horn. Read jiǎo for horn, corner and angle; jué for a role, as in 角色.
艹 (grass, plants) — plants and leaves: 花, 草, 叶; 落 is leaves falling.
洛 (luò) sounds exactly like 落; related to 各 gè in 路 lù.

example.hanzi: 猫躲在房间的角落里睡觉。
example.pinyin: Māo duǒ zài fángjiān de jiǎoluò lǐ shuìjiào.
example.english: The cat is hiding in the corner of the room, sleeping.
example.fact: A 2014 study on shelter cats found that cats given an enclosed hiding box adjusted to a new environment and showed lower stress-hormone levels faster than cats without one, supporting the idea that cats instinctively seek tight, corner-like spaces to feel secure.

examples.hanzi: 我的钥匙掉在了角落里。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de yàoshi diào zài le jiǎoluò lǐ.
examples.english: My key fell into a corner.

examples.hanzi: 这个咖啡馆的角落很安静。
examples.pinyin: Zhège kāfēiguǎn de jiǎoluò hěn ānjìng.
examples.english: The corner of this cafe is very quiet.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — marks the head and face, as in 顶, 题, 顺; 预 is thinking ahead.
予 (yǔ) hints at the sound: 预 yù is close, as in 豫 yù.
言 (speech) — 言 is the traditional full form of the 讠 radical for speech and language: 说, 话, 语, 请.

example.hanzi: 他的预言最后竟然成真了。
example.pinyin: Tā de yùyán zuìhòu jìngrán chéngzhēn le.
example.english: His prophecy actually came true in the end.
example.fact: Ancient Greeks traveled across the Mediterranean to consult the Oracle of Delphi, a priestess called the Pythia who delivered prophecies in a trance. Modern geological studies suggest fissures beneath the temple may have released ethylene gas, which could help explain her altered state.

examples.hanzi: 没有人能预言未来。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu rén néng yùyán wèilái.
examples.english: No one can predict the future.

examples.hanzi: 这个古老的预言流传了几百年。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gǔlǎo de yùyán liúchuán le jǐ bǎi nián.
examples.english: This ancient prophecy has been passed down for hundreds of years.

components.note: 异 (simplified 異) — means different or strange; its yì sound also appears in 翼 yì (wing).

example.hanzi: 两国的文化差异很大。
example.pinyin: Liǎng guó de wénhuà chāyì hěn dà.
example.english: The cultures of the two countries differ greatly.
example.fact: 异 is the simplified form of 異 and means 'different' or 'strange'. It builds 差异 (difference), 异常 (abnormal), 惊异 and 异国 (a foreign land); it is mostly written, not spoken.

examples.hanzi: 他对这个结果感到惊异。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì zhège jiéguǒ gǎndào jīngyì.
examples.english: He was amazed by this result.

examples.hanzi: 你身体有什么异常吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shēntǐ yǒu shénme yìcháng ma?
examples.english: Is anything unusual with your body?

components.note: 氵 (water) — water leaking through; also in 河 river, 海 sea.
屚 (lòu) — rain (雨) under a roof (尸): a leaking roof. It gives the sound and also sounds out 陋 lòu.

example.hanzi: 屋顶漏水了。
example.pinyin: Wūdǐng lòu shuǐ le.
example.english: The roof is leaking.
example.fact: 漏 means both 'to leak' (漏水, 漏气) and, figuratively, 'to omit, to miss': 漏了一个字 is 'missed a word'. 泄漏 and 漏洞 (loophole, security hole) are common in news and tech.

examples.hanzi: 你漏写了一个汉字。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ lòu xiě le yí ge Hànzì.
examples.english: You left out a Chinese character.

examples.hanzi: 这个杯子漏水了,快拿块布来。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bēizi lòu shuǐ le, kuài ná kuài bù lái.
examples.english: This cup is leaking; quick, bring a cloth.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
师 (shī) is a sound clue for 狮 shī (lion) and 筛 shāi; as a word it means master or teacher.

example.hanzi: 他是国际知名的围棋大师。
example.pinyin: Tā shì guójì zhīmíng de wéiqí dàshī.
example.english: He is an internationally renowned Go master.
example.fact: The board game Go has more possible board positions than there are atoms in the observable universe, an estimate as high as 10^170, which is a major reason computers struggled to master it until AlphaGo's breakthrough win in 2016.

examples.hanzi: 这位大师画的画非常有名。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi dàshī huà de huà fēicháng yǒumíng.
examples.english: The paintings by this master are very famous.

examples.hanzi: 他拜了一位书法大师为师。
examples.pinyin: Tā bài le yí wèi shūfǎ dàshī wéi shī.
examples.english: He took a calligraphy master as his teacher.

components.note: 气 (air, vapor) — lines of rising vapor or breath. Add water for 汽 steam; seen in 生气 get angry, 空气 air.
气 (vapour) — marks air and gas, as in 汽, 氧 oxygen, 气; 氛 is the air or mood.
分 (fēn) gives the sound exactly: 氛 fēn, as in 气氛.

example.hanzi: 派对上的气氛非常热烈。
example.pinyin: Pàiduì shàng de qìfēn fēicháng rèliè.
example.english: The atmosphere at the party was very lively.
example.fact: Earth's atmosphere has no sharp edge, but the internationally recognized boundary of space, the Kármán line, is set at 100 kilometers altitude — above which conventional aircraft can no longer generate enough lift, and vehicles must switch to rocket propulsion instead.

examples.hanzi: 教室里的气氛很轻松。
examples.pinyin: Jiàoshì lǐ de qìfēn hěn qīngsōng.
examples.english: The atmosphere in the classroom is relaxed.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅的气氛很浪漫。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de qìfēn hěn làngmàn.
examples.english: The atmosphere in this restaurant is very romantic.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 按; 批 is to strike, then to comment.
比 (bǐ) is a loose hint for pī.
冫 (ice) — cold, as in 冷 cold, 冰 ice, 冻 freeze; here it stands for 氵 water in 準 (a water level, so exact).
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) gives only a loose sound clue for zhǔn.

example.hanzi: 这项计划已经得到政府批准。
example.pinyin: Zhè xiàng jìhuà yǐjīng dédào zhèngfǔ pīzhǔn.
example.english: This plan has already received government approval.
example.fact: Getting a new drug approved in the United States takes on average more than a decade and costs upward of a billion dollars, largely because roughly 90% of drug candidates that enter clinical trials fail somewhere along the way and never reach approval.

examples.hanzi: 经理批准了我的假期申请。
examples.pinyin: Jīnglǐ pīzhǔn le wǒ de jiàqī shēnqǐng.
examples.english: The manager approved my vacation request.

examples.hanzi: 这个方案还没有被批准。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fāng'àn hái méiyǒu bèi pīzhǔn.
examples.english: This proposal has not been approved yet.

components.note: 青 (qīng) hints at the -ing rhyme; same part in 清 请 情 晴 精. The 争 (contend) half is not a reliable clue.

example.hanzi: 图书馆里很静。
example.pinyin: Túshūguǎn lǐ hěn jìng.
example.english: It is very quiet in the library.
example.fact: 静 is quieter than 安静 only in tone: 请安静 is the normal polite 'be quiet', while 静 mostly forms compounds: 平静 (calm), 冷静 (composed), 寂静 (silent) and 静止 (still).

examples.hanzi: 请保持安静。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎochí ānjìng.
examples.english: Please keep quiet.

examples.hanzi: 夜晚的村子很平静。
examples.pinyin: Yèwǎn de cūnzi hěn píngjìng.
examples.english: The village is very peaceful at night.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — the body-part radical, as in 肝 liver, 脸, 腿; 脾 is the spleen, and by extension temper.
卑 (bēi) hints at the sound: 脾 pí is close to 牌 pái and 啤 pí.
气 (air, vapor) — lines of rising vapor or breath. Add water for 汽 steam; seen in 生气 get angry, 空气 air.

example.hanzi: 他的脾气一向很好。
example.pinyin: Tā de píqi yīxiàng hěn hǎo.
example.english: He has always had a good temper.
example.fact: When a person becomes angry, the brain's amygdala can trigger a stress response in well under a second, releasing adrenaline before the slower, more rational prefrontal cortex has time to weigh in — part of why deliberately pausing before reacting actually gives the rational brain a chance to catch up.

examples.hanzi: 他的脾气很大，容易生气。
examples.pinyin: Tā de píqi hěn dà, róngyì shēngqì.
examples.english: He has a bad temper and gets angry easily.

examples.hanzi: 你别发脾气，慢慢说。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié fā píqi, mànmàn shuō.
examples.english: Don't lose your temper; speak slowly.

components.note: 石 (stone) — marks stone and hard things, as in 破, 码, 砖; 碎 is to smash into bits.
卒 (zú) hints at the sound: 碎 suì is close to 醉 zuì and 翠 cuì.
片 (slice) — the right half of 木 split down the middle: a flat piece. See 版 bǎn (printing plate) and 牌 pái (card).

example.hanzi: 花瓶摔碎后留下了一地碎片。
example.pinyin: Huāpíng shuāisuì hòu liúxiàle yī dì suìpiàn.
example.english: After the vase shattered, fragments were left all over the floor.
example.fact: The European Space Agency estimates there are more than 130 million pieces of space debris smaller than a centimeter orbiting Earth, remnants of old satellites and rockets — even a paint fleck traveling at orbital speeds of roughly 28,000 km/h can damage a spacecraft.

examples.hanzi: 地上有玻璃碎片，小心点。
examples.pinyin: Dì shàng yǒu bōlí suìpiàn, xiǎoxīn diǎn.
examples.english: There are glass fragments on the floor, so be careful.

examples.hanzi: 他把照片的碎片拼了起来。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ zhàopiàn de suìpiàn pīn le qǐlai.
examples.english: He pieced the fragments of the photo back together.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
罒 (net, form of 网) — nets and entrapment: 罗 net, 罚 punish, 骂 scold; here a net of wrongdoing 非 catching the guilty.
非 (not, wrong) — what is wrong or unlawful; in 罪 it is the wrongdoing caught in the net.

example.hanzi: 法院最终判他无罪。
example.pinyin: Fǎyuàn zuìzhōng pàn tā wúzuì.
example.english: The court ultimately found him not guilty.
example.fact: Since 1992, the Innocence Project has used DNA evidence to help exonerate more than 375 wrongfully convicted people in the United States, some of whom had already spent decades in prison, including time on death row.

examples.hanzi: 大家都相信他是无罪的。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu xiāngxìn tā shì wúzuì de.
examples.english: Everyone believes he is innocent.

examples.hanzi: 法官宣布被告无罪。
examples.pinyin: Fǎguān xuānbù bèigào wúzuì.
examples.english: The judge declared the defendant not guilty.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 逃 is to run away.
兆 (zhào) — loose hint — 逃 is táo; 兆 also sounds out 桃 táo (same sound) and 跳 tiào.
月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the body radical (月 in 脸, 脑); 脱 is slipping off a layer, like skin or clothes.
兑 (duì) — near sound — 脱 is tuō; 兑 also sounds out 说 shuō and 税 shuì.

example.hanzi: 那只鸟趁机逃脱了笼子。
example.pinyin: Nà zhī niǎo chènjī táotuōle lóngzi.
example.english: That bird seized the chance to escape the cage.
example.fact: Octopuses are famous escape artists because they have no rigid skeleton and can squeeze through any opening larger than their beak, the one hard part of their body — a New Zealand octopus named Inky made international news in 2016 after sliding down a drainpipe back to the ocean.

examples.hanzi: 他从火场里成功逃脱了。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng huǒchǎng lǐ chénggōng táotuō le.
examples.english: He successfully escaped from the fire.

examples.hanzi: 这个游戏里你要想办法逃脱。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yóuxì lǐ nǐ yào xiǎng bànfǎ táotuō.
examples.english: In this game, you have to find a way to escape.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical (单人旁) — 价 is about what people pay or the worth of things; also in 你, 他, 住.
介 (jiè) — near-sound hint — 价 is jià; 介 also sounds out 界 jiè and 阶 jiē.
木 (wood, tree) — wood radical — 格 first meant a wooden frame or lattice, hence "pattern, standard"; compare 树 tree, 板 board.
各 (gè) — same syllable, different tone — 格 is gé; 各 also sounds out 阁 gé and 胳 gē.

example.hanzi: 这台电脑的价格比我想象的便宜。
example.pinyin: Zhè tái diànnǎo de jiàgé bǐ wǒ xiǎngxiàng de piányí.
example.english: This computer's price is cheaper than I imagined.
example.fact: Moore's Law, the 1965 observation that the number of transistors on a computer chip roughly doubles every two years, held remarkably true for decades and is a major reason computing power that once cost millions of dollars now fits in a phone costing a few hundred.

examples.hanzi: 这件衣服的价格太贵了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu de jiàgé tài guì le.
examples.english: The price of this garment is too expensive.

examples.hanzi: 请问这个价格包括运费吗？
examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn zhège jiàgé bāokuò yùnfèi ma?
examples.english: Excuse me, does this price include shipping?

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — marks bamboo and things made of it, as in 笔, 筷, 签; 策 was a bamboo whip or slip, then a plan.
朿 (cì) hints at the sound: 策 cè is close.
各 (gè) is only a loose hint for lüè; 路 lù and 络 luò share it.

example.hanzi: 教练在比赛中改变了策略。
example.pinyin: Jiàoliàn zài bǐsài zhōng gǎibiànle cèlüè.
example.english: The coach changed strategy during the match.
example.fact: In 1950, mathematician John Nash proved that any competitive game with a finite number of players and strategies has at least one stable outcome, now called a Nash equilibrium, where no player can benefit by changing strategy alone — the insight later won him a Nobel Prize in Economics.

examples.hanzi: 我们需要一个新的营销策略。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào yí ge xīn de yíngxiāo cèlüè.
examples.english: We need a new marketing strategy.

examples.hanzi: 他用聪明的策略赢了这局棋。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng cōngming de cèlüè yíng le zhè jú qí.
examples.english: He won this game of chess with a clever strategy.

components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.

example.hanzi: 街角坐着一个老头在下棋。
example.pinyin: Jiējiǎo zuòzhe yī gè lǎotóu zài xiàqí.
example.english: An old man is sitting at the street corner playing chess.
example.fact: The longest officially recorded chess game lasted 269 moves and over 20 hours before ending in a draw, played between Ivan Nikolić and Goran Arsović in Belgrade in 1989 — arbiters eventually had to step in to bring it to a close.

examples.hanzi: 那个老头每天早上都来公园。
examples.pinyin: Nàge lǎotóu měitiān zǎoshang dōu lái gōngyuán.
examples.english: That old man comes to the park every morning.

examples.hanzi: 我家隔壁住着一个和气的老头。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā gébì zhù zhe yí ge héqi de lǎotóu.
examples.english: A friendly old man lives next door to us.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 嘻 is a laughing sound, as in 笑嘻嘻.
喜 (xǐ) — close sound: 嘻 xī. 喜 means joy, fitting a giggle.

example.hanzi: 孩子嘻嘻地笑了。
example.pinyin: Háizi xīxī de xiào le.
example.english: The child laughed with a giggle.
example.fact: 嘻 is an onomatopoeic syllable for giggling; doubled as 嘻嘻 (heehee) or in 笑嘻嘻 'beaming'. It is also the first half of 嘻哈, the transliteration of 'hip-hop'.

examples.hanzi: 他嘻嘻地笑个不停。
examples.pinyin: Tā xīxī de xiào ge bù tíng.
examples.english: He giggled nonstop.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们嘻嘻哈哈地跑出去了。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen xīxīhāhā de pǎo chūqù le.
examples.english: The kids ran out laughing and playing.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.
告 (gào) — loose hint — 靠 is kào; 告 also sounds out 造 zào and 酷 kù.
非 (not) — two wings pointing away from each other, so back to back; as a memory aid, 靠 is leaning your back on something.

example.hanzi: 这台机器的性能非常可靠。
example.pinyin: Zhè tái jīqì de xìngnéng fēicháng kěkào.
example.english: This machine's performance is very reliable.
example.fact: The Voyager 1 spacecraft, launched in 1977 with computer technology far less powerful than a modern calculator, is still transmitting data from interstellar space more than 47 years later, a testament to conservative, redundant engineering built to far outlast its original mission.

examples.hanzi: 他是个可靠的人，你可以放心。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì ge kěkào de rén, nǐ kěyǐ fàngxīn.
examples.english: He's a reliable person; you can relax.

examples.hanzi: 这个消息来源可靠吗？
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi láiyuán kěkào ma?
examples.english: Is the source of this news reliable?

components.note: 页 (head) — 页 is the head, as in 题, 顶, 颜; 领 is the neck and then to lead.
令 (lìng) — near sound — 领 is lǐng; 令 also sounds out 龄 líng and 铃 líng.
儿 (legs, person) — with a foot 𠂉 above: a foot stepping out in front of a person, so "first, earlier".

example.hanzi: 我们的团队目前在比赛中领先。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen de tuánduì mùqián zài bǐsài zhōng lǐngxiān.
example.english: Our team is currently leading in the competition.
example.fact: Usain Bolt's 100-meter world record of 9.58 seconds, set in 2009, works out to an average speed of over 37 km/h, with radar tracking showing his peak speed during the race topping 44 km/h — faster than many neighborhood speed limits.

examples.hanzi: 我们队在上半场领先两分。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen duì zài shàng bàn chǎng lǐngxiān liǎng fēn.
examples.english: Our team led by two points in the first half.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司的技术领先于同行。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī de jìshù lǐngxiān yú tóngháng.
examples.english: This company's technology is ahead of its competitors.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — clothes and wear: 衬, 被, 袋; 装 is dress, then to pretend or to load.
壮 (zhuàng) is a near sound match for zhuāng; also in 状 zhuàng and 妆 zhuāng.
田 (field) — the bottom part. 备 is simplified from 備; the dictionary story is a trip to the 田 field to prepare for harvest. Treat it as a memory aid.
夂 (going down, slow step) — the top. Memory aid: heading 夂 to the field 田 to get ready — 准备, 设备.

example.hanzi: 登山队检查了所有装备才出发。
example.pinyin: Dēngshān duì jiǎnchále suǒyǒu zhuāngbèi cái chūfā.
example.english: The mountaineering team checked all their equipment before setting out.
example.fact: Climbers on Mount Everest typically carry supplemental oxygen above 8,000 meters, an altitude nicknamed the 'death zone,' where air pressure is only about a third of sea level — too little oxygen for the human body to ever fully acclimatize, no matter how long it stays.

examples.hanzi: 消防员穿上了全套装备。
examples.pinyin: Xiāofángyuán chuān shàng le quántào zhuāngbèi.
examples.english: The firefighters put on their full set of gear.

examples.hanzi: 他们给军队装备了新武器。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen gěi jūnduì zhuāngbèi le xīn wǔqì.
examples.english: They equipped the army with new weapons.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 体 is a person's body.
本 (root) — the root of a person, the body; the traditional form was 體 with 骨 (bone).
马 (horse) — horses: 骑, 驾, 骄; 验 first meant testing a horse, then any test.
佥 (qiān) gives the -ian rhyme; same part in 险 xiǎn, 检 jiǎn, 脸 liǎn, 签 qiān.

example.hanzi: 这次旅行让我体验到了不同的文化。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì lǚxíng ràng wǒ tǐyàn dàole bùtóng de wénhuà.
example.english: This trip let me experience a different culture.
example.fact: Memory researchers describe a 'holiday paradox': new, unfamiliar experiences get encoded with far more detail than routine ones, so a novel trip can feel like it flew by while it's happening but feel much longer than a week at home when you look back on it.

examples.hanzi: 我想体验一下当地的生活。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng tǐyàn yíxià dāngdì de shēnghuó.
examples.english: I'd like to experience local life.

examples.hanzi: 这个游戏的体验很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yóuxì de tǐyàn hěn hǎo.
examples.english: The experience of this game is great.

components.note: 亲 (qīn) keeps the sound part of the traditional 親, which also had 见; it also gives 新 xīn and 薪 xīn, so qīn/xīn is a series.
友 (friend) replaces the heart-and-foot lower part of the traditional 愛, which had 心 (heart); so 爱 lost its heart in simplification.
白 (white, bright) — 的 first meant bright and clear, as in 的确 dí què.
勺 (sháo) is a loose sound clue for dì; 勺 also sounds out 约 yuē and 钓 diào.

example.hanzi: 亲爱的,晚饭已经准备好了。
example.pinyin: Qīn'ài de, wǎnfàn yǐjīng zhǔnbèi hǎo le.
example.english: Darling, dinner is already ready.
example.fact: Relationship research has found that couples who regularly use private pet names and terms of endearment for each other tend to report higher relationship satisfaction, since the small shared ritual reinforces a sense of private, exclusive identity between partners.

examples.hanzi: 亲爱的朋友，你好吗？
examples.pinyin: Qīn'ài de péngyou, nǐ hǎo ma?
examples.english: Dear friend, how are you?

examples.hanzi: 亲爱的，别忘了带钥匙。
examples.pinyin: Qīn'ài de, bié wàng le dài yàoshi.
examples.english: Dear, don't forget to take your keys.

components.note: 土 (earth) — soil and land: 地, 场, 块; 坏 first meant to collapse, as of a wall of earth.
不 (bù) is only a stand-in for the old sound part 褱 (huái); a loose clue for huài.
虫 (insect, creature) — small animals and insects, as in 蚊 mosquito, 蛇 snake, 虾 shrimp: 蛋 is the egg of a creature.

example.hanzi: 电影里的坏蛋最后被警察抓住了。
example.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de huàidàn zuìhòu bèi jǐngchá zhuāzhù le.
example.english: The villain in the movie was finally caught by the police.
example.fact: A simple way to test whether an egg is still fresh is to drop it in water: a fresh egg sinks and lies flat, while an old one floats upright or on its side, because the air pocket inside grows larger over time as moisture escapes and air seeps in through the shell's pores.

examples.hanzi: 你这个小坏蛋，又偷吃糖了！
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhège xiǎo huàidàn, yòu tōu chī táng le!
examples.english: You little rascal, you sneaked candy again!

examples.hanzi: 这个坏蛋骗了很多人。
examples.pinyin: Zhège huàidàn piàn le hěn duō rén.
examples.english: This scoundrel has deceived many people.

components.note: 糸 (silk, simplified 纟) — undyed silk: plain and basic, hence 元素 element and 素食 vegetarian fare.

example.hanzi: 我吃素，不吃肉。
example.pinyin: Wǒ chī sù, bù chī ròu.
example.english: I'm a vegetarian; I don't eat meat.
example.fact: 素 originally meant undyed raw silk, hence 'plain, unadorned'. It forms 吃素 (to eat vegetarian), 素菜, 素质 (quality) and 元素 (element), and is the opposite of 荤 (meat-based).

examples.hanzi: 我今天想吃素菜。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān xiǎng chī sùcài.
examples.english: I want to eat vegetarian dishes today.

examples.hanzi: 多吃蔬菜可以补充维生素。
examples.pinyin: Duō chī shūcài kěyǐ bǔchōng wéishēngsù.
examples.english: Eating more vegetables supplies vitamins.

components.note: 中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.
午 (noon) — an old picture of a pestle or mallet, later borrowed for 'noon'. Memory aid: noon is when the sun stands straight overhead — 下午, 午饭.

example.hanzi: 我们中午一起去吃饭吧。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōngwǔ yīqǐ qù chīfàn ba.
example.english: Let's go eat together at noon.
example.fact: 'Solar noon,' the moment the sun reaches its highest point in the sky, rarely matches 12:00 on a clock exactly — it can shift by up to about 16 minutes either way over the course of a year, a discrepancy called the equation of time, caused by Earth's elliptical orbit and axial tilt.

examples.hanzi: 中午十二点我们在食堂见。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngwǔ shí'èr diǎn wǒmen zài shítáng jiàn.
examples.english: Let's meet at the cafeteria at twelve noon.

examples.hanzi: 我中午通常睡一会儿。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhōngwǔ tōngcháng shuì yíhuìr.
examples.english: I usually take a short nap at noon.

components.note: 录 (lù) gives sound to 绿 lǜ, 禄 lù and 碌 lù; as a word it means to record.
音 (sound) — 言 (speech) with a stroke inside the mouth: a note within speech. 音 also gives 意 yì and 暗 àn.

example.hanzi: 他把整个会议都录音了下来。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ zhěnggè huìyì dōu lùyīnle xiàlái.
example.english: He recorded the entire meeting.
example.fact: The oldest known recording of a human voice that can still be played back today is a 10-second phonautogram made in 1860 by Édouard-Léon Scott de Martinville, seventeen years before Edison's phonograph — it was only successfully played back in 2008 after being scanned and converted to digital audio.

examples.hanzi: 我想录音，这样回去可以再听。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng lùyīn, zhèyàng huíqù kěyǐ zài tīng.
examples.english: I want to record it so I can listen again when I get back.

examples.hanzi: 这段录音很清楚。
examples.pinyin: Zhè duàn lùyīn hěn qīngchu.
examples.english: This recording is very clear.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — fire and heat, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 黑 black: light shining.
昭 (zhāo) is a close sound clue for zhào; 昭 itself means bright.
手 (hand) — over 目 (eye): a hand shading the eyes to look into the distance. 目 marks seeing words, as in 眼, 睡.

example.hanzi: 奶奶在家照看小孙子。
example.pinyin: Nǎinai zàijiā zhàokàn xiǎo sūnzi.
example.english: Grandma is looking after her little grandson at home.
example.fact: Large-scale surveys on aging have found that roughly two in five grandparents provide regular childcare for their grandchildren, and researchers have linked active grandparenting to measurable benefits for both grandparents' cognitive health and grandchildren's social development.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈出门时，我来照看弟弟。
examples.pinyin: Māma chūmén shí, wǒ lái zhàokàn dìdi.
examples.english: When Mom goes out, I look after my little brother.

examples.hanzi: 请帮我照看一下行李。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ zhàokàn yíxià xíngli.
examples.english: Please keep an eye on my luggage for me.

components.note: 阝 (mound, hill) — left-side 阝 is 阜 (mound), as in 阳, 院; 阿 first meant a slope.
可 (kě) — near sound — 阿 is ā; 可 also sounds out 河 hé and 哥 gē.
门 (gate) — a picture of a two-leaf door; as a radical it frames characters of doors and openings — 开, 关, 问, 间.

example.hanzi: 牧师祷告结束后,大家一起说:"阿门。"
example.pinyin: Mùshī dǎogào jiéshù hòu, dàjiā yīqǐ shuō: "Āmén."
example.english: After the pastor finished the prayer, everyone said together, "Amen."
example.fact: The word 'amen' comes from Biblical Hebrew, where it means roughly 'so be it' or 'truly.' It has been carried, largely unchanged in pronunciation, across Judaism, Christianity, and Islam for more than two thousand years, making it one of the most widely shared loanwords among unrelated religious traditions.

examples.hanzi: 大家一起祈祷，最后说“阿门”。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā yìqǐ qídǎo, zuìhòu shuō "āmén".
examples.english: Everyone prayed together and finally said "Amen."

examples.hanzi: 教堂里传来了“阿门”的声音。
examples.pinyin: Jiàotáng lǐ chuánlái le "āmén" de shēngyīn.
examples.english: The sound of "Amen" came from the church.

components.note: 贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is money, as in 买, 财, 费; 货 is goods that are traded.
化 (huà) — near sound — 货 is huò; 化 also sounds out 花 huā.
车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.

example.hanzi: 一辆货车正在卸货。
example.pinyin: Yī liàng huòchē zhèngzài xièhuò.
example.english: A truck is unloading goods.
example.fact: The U.S. Interstate Highway System, the backbone of modern long-haul trucking, was partly inspired by Germany's autobahn network, which Dwight Eisenhower had seen during World War II. Its construction, beginning in 1956, was the largest public works project in American history at the time.

examples.hanzi: 这辆货车装满了苹果。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng huòchē zhuāng mǎn le píngguǒ.
examples.english: This truck is loaded full of apples.

examples.hanzi: 货车司机在路边休息。
examples.pinyin: Huòchē sījī zài lùbiān xiūxi.
examples.english: The truck driver is resting by the roadside.

components.note: 彳 (step) — walking and going, as in 行, 往, 很 very.
寸 (hand) — oldest form is a hand grabbing a cowrie shell (money): 得 is "to obtain". The shell has worn down to 旦.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.

example.hanzi: 他在最后一秒钟得分,帮球队赢了比赛。
example.pinyin: Tā zài zuìhòu yī miǎozhōng défēn, bāng qiúduì yíngle bǐsài.
example.english: He scored in the final second, helping the team win the game.
example.fact: In basketball, a shot only counts if the ball leaves the shooter's hand before the game clock reads zero — a rule now enforced with camera systems precise enough to review fractions of a second, adopted across major leagues after several famously disputed buzzer-beater calls in the 1990s.

examples.hanzi: 他今天比赛得分最高。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān bǐsài défēn zuì gāo.
examples.english: He had the highest score in today's game.

examples.hanzi: 这次考试我没有得分。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì wǒ méiyǒu défēn.
examples.english: I got no points on this exam.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, from 糸) — marks thread and weaving, as in 线, 红, 绳; 编 is to weave, then to compile.
扁 (biǎn) gives the sound: 编 biān is close, as in 偏 piān and 篇 piān.
车 (cart, vehicle) — marks wheeled things, as in 转, 轮, 较; 辑 originally meant carriage parts, then gathering and editing.

example.hanzi: 她是一家杂志的编辑。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yī jiā zázhì de biānjí.
example.english: She is an editor at a magazine.
example.fact: Before word processors, editors marked up manuscripts using a standardized set of proofreading symbols, many still taught today, that trace back to conventions developed by print shops in the 15th and 16th centuries, not long after Gutenberg's press made mass-produced text possible.

examples.hanzi: 他在出版社当编辑。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài chūbǎnshè dāng biānjí.
examples.english: He works as an editor at a publishing house.

examples.hanzi: 请帮我编辑一下这份文件。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ biānjí yíxià zhè fèn wénjiàn.
examples.english: Please help me edit this document.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings and thinking: 想 think, 思, 感 feel, 忙; forgetting is a loss of the heart's hold.
亡 (wáng, lose) gives the sound and fits the sense: to lose from the mind.
扌 (hand) — hand radical for actions — 掉 is to drop or lose hold.

example.hanzi: 她努力想忘掉那段痛苦的记忆。
example.pinyin: Tā nǔlì xiǎng wàngdiào nà duàn tòngkǔ de jìyì.
example.english: She tried hard to forget that painful memory.
example.fact: In the 1880s, psychologist Hermann Ebbinghaus tested his own memory and mapped out the 'forgetting curve': without any review, people forget over half of newly learned information within about an hour, and up to 70% within a day — a finding that still underlies modern spaced-repetition study techniques.

examples.hanzi: 我想忘掉今天发生的事。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng wàngdiào jīntiān fāshēng de shì.
examples.english: I want to forget what happened today.

examples.hanzi: 这么重要的约会，你怎么能忘掉？
examples.pinyin: Zhème zhòngyào de yuēhuì, nǐ zěnme néng wàngdiào?
examples.english: How could you forget such an important appointment?

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 情, 快, 怕; 性 is the inner nature of a thing.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint; also in 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
木 (wood, tree) — wood radical — 格 first meant a wooden frame or lattice, hence "pattern, standard"; compare 树 tree, 板 board.
各 (gè) — same syllable, different tone — 格 is gé; 各 also sounds out 阁 gé and 胳 gē.

example.hanzi: 她的性格开朗又乐观。
example.pinyin: Tā de xìnggé kāilǎng yòu lèguān.
example.english: Her personality is cheerful and optimistic.
example.fact: Modern psychology's most widely used personality framework, the 'Big Five,' measures traits across just five broad dimensions — openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, and neuroticism — and twin studies suggest genetics accounts for roughly 40 to 60% of the variation in these traits between people.

examples.hanzi: 她的性格比较内向。
examples.pinyin: Tā de xìnggé bǐjiào nèixiàng.
examples.english: Her personality is rather introverted.

examples.hanzi: 兄弟俩的性格完全不同。
examples.pinyin: Xiōngdì liǎ de xìnggé wánquán bù tóng.
examples.english: The two brothers have completely different personalities.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海, 汤; 流 is flowing water.
㐬 (liú) — same sound — 流 is liú; 㐬 also sounds out 琉 liú and 硫 liú.
亡 (wáng) hints at the sound: 氓 máng is close to 忙 máng and 盲 máng, which share it.

example.hanzi: 警察逮捕了几个街头流氓。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá dàibǔle jǐ gè jiētóu liúmáng.
example.english: Police arrested a few street hoodlums.
example.fact: Criminologists studying urban violence have found it is highly concentrated geographically — in some U.S. cities, over half of all gun violence occurs on less than 5% of city blocks, a pattern that let 'focused deterrence' policing strategies target resources far more precisely than city-wide patrols.

examples.hanzi: 别和街上的流氓来往。
examples.pinyin: Bié hé jiē shàng de liúmáng láiwǎng.
examples.english: Don't associate with the thugs on the street.

examples.hanzi: 那几个流氓在巷子里捣乱。
examples.pinyin: Nà jǐ ge liúmáng zài xiàngzi lǐ dǎoluàn.
examples.english: Those few hoodlums are causing trouble in the alley.

components.note: 犭 (dog, beast) — animals: 狗, 猫, 狼; 独 first meant a solitary animal, then alone.
The old sound part 蜀 (shǔ) is also in 属 shǔ, 烛 zhú and 触 chù; simplified 独 shows 虫 instead.
舛 (two opposed feet) — the dancer's footwork; 無 (wú) above is a loose sound clue, as it once meant dance itself.

example.hanzi: 她在晚会上表演了一段独舞。
example.pinyin: Tā zài wǎnhuì shàng biǎoyǎnle yī duàn dúwǔ.
example.english: She performed a solo dance at the evening party.
example.fact: One of classical ballet's most demanding solo passages, the Black Swan's coda in Swan Lake, requires 32 consecutive fouetté turns performed in place — a feat that pushes a dancer's balance and rotational stamina to its limits.

examples.hanzi: 她从小学舞蹈，最喜欢独舞。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo xué wǔdǎo, zuì xǐhuan dúwǔ.
examples.english: She has studied dance since childhood and likes solo dances best.

examples.hanzi: 这场独舞表演得很精彩。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng dúwǔ biǎoyǎn de hěn jīngcǎi.
examples.english: This solo dance was performed brilliantly.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 优 first meant a person who performs or is excellent, in 演员 and 优秀.
尤 (yóu) — near sound — 优 is yōu; 尤 also sounds out 忧 yōu.
力 (strength) — 力 is strength, as in 办, 动, 努; 势 is force or momentum.

example.hanzi: 他在比赛中占据优势。
example.pinyin: tā zài bǐsài zhōng zhànjù yōushì.
example.english: He has the advantage in the competition.
example.fact: Monarch butterflies store toxic compounds from the milkweed they eat as caterpillars, making them poisonous to most predators. Birds that eat one quickly learn to avoid the bright orange pattern, giving monarchs a lasting survival advantage. This defense is so effective that other harmless butterfly species, like the viceroy, evolved to mimic its coloring.

examples.hanzi: 我们的产品在价格上有优势。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de chǎnpǐn zài jiàgé shàng yǒu yōushì.
examples.english: Our product has an advantage in price.

examples.hanzi: 他身高很高，打篮球有优势。
examples.pinyin: Tā shēngāo hěn gāo, dǎ lánqiú yǒu yōushì.
examples.english: He's tall, which gives him an edge in basketball.

components.note: 聲 (traditional) — a hanging stone chime struck, with 耳 (ear) below: a sound you hear. 声 keeps only the top, so the picture is mostly lost.
士 (scholar) — the top of 声 is only a leftover of the old chime, not 'scholar'. Do not read meaning into it.
日 (sun) — the sun beside the moon: two light sources, so bright and clear.
月 (moon) — as in 朋, 期, 有; here it brightens the night.

example.hanzi: 公司发布了一份声明。
example.pinyin: gōngsī fābù le yī fèn shēngmíng.
example.english: The company issued a statement.
example.fact: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in Paris on December 10, 1948, in the aftermath of World War II. Eleanor Roosevelt chaired the drafting committee and pushed for a document that could apply across vastly different legal and cultural systems. It remains the most translated document in the world, available in over 500 languages.

examples.hanzi: 他们对这件事发表了联合声明。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen duì zhè jiàn shì fābiǎo le liánhé shēngmíng.
examples.english: They issued a joint statement on this matter.

examples.hanzi: 他声明自己不会参加比赛。
examples.pinyin: Tā shēngmíng zìjǐ bú huì cānjiā bǐsài.
examples.english: He declared that he would not take part in the competition.

components.note: 饣 (food, from 食) — marks food, as in 饭, 饿, 饼; 馅 is the filling of a dumpling or pie.
臽 (xiàn) gives the sound exactly: 馅 xiàn, also in 陷 xiàn.
饣 (food) — 饣 is the simplified 食 (food), as in 饭, 饺, 饿; 饼 is a flat baked cake.
并 (bìng) — near sound — 饼 is bǐng; 并 also sounds out 拼 pīn.

example.hanzi: 妈妈做了苹果馅饼。
example.pinyin: māma zuò le píngguǒ xiànbǐng.
example.english: Mom made an apple pie.
example.fact: Pies date back at least 4,000 years: ancient Egyptians baked early versions using a mixture of oats, wheat, rye, or barley filled with honey. The ancient Greeks are credited with developing the first pastry crust to hold a filling, a technique the Romans later spread across their empire. Meat pies became especially common in medieval Europe, where the crust doubled as an edible container for traveling meals.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的馅饼是用牛肉做的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de xiànbǐng shì yòng niúròu zuò de.
examples.english: The pies at this shop are made with beef.

examples.hanzi: 我早餐吃了一个韭菜馅饼。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zǎocān chī le yí ge jiǔcài xiànbǐng.
examples.english: I had a chive pie for breakfast.

components.note: 彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.hanzi: 他一向按规矩行事。
example.pinyin: tā yīxiàng àn guīju xíngshì.
example.english: He always acts according to the rules.
example.fact: The Code of Hammurabi, carved around 1754 BC onto a black diorite stele nearly 2.25 meters tall, is one of the oldest deciphered writings of significant length in the world. It laid out nearly 300 laws covering trade, family, and criminal conduct, with punishments that famously varied by the social status of those involved. The stele was rediscovered in 1901 in present-day Iran and is now displayed in the Louvre.

examples.hanzi: 他做事谨慎，行事低调。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuòshì jǐnshèn, xíngshì dīdiào.
examples.english: He is careful and acts in a low-key way.

examples.hanzi: 你要按计划行事，别乱来。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào àn jìhuà xíngshì, bié luànlái.
examples.english: You must act according to the plan and not mess around.

components.note: 临 (simplified 臨) — the old form shows a person bending over with a watching eye above a heap of goods: looking down on something, hence 'to face, to draw near'.
日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.hanzi: 这只是一个临时办法。
example.pinyin: zhè zhǐshì yī gè línshí bànfǎ.
example.english: This is only a temporary solution.
example.fact: The Eiffel Tower was built for the 1889 World's Fair in Paris and was only meant to stand for 20 years before being dismantled. Gustave Eiffel saved it by pointing out its usefulness for radio transmissions, and the city ultimately let it stay. Today it draws about 7 million visitors a year, making the 'temporary' structure one of the most visited monuments on Earth.

examples.hanzi: 会议临时取消了。
examples.pinyin: Huìyì línshí qǔxiāo le.
examples.english: The meeting was cancelled at the last minute.

examples.hanzi: 我临时有点事，晚点到。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ línshí yǒudiǎn shì, wǎndiǎn dào.
examples.english: Something came up at the last minute, so I'll arrive a bit late.

components.note: 黄 (huáng) — yellow; as a part it sounds out 簧 huáng and 磺 huáng.
今 (jīn) — the top part hints the sound — 金 is jīn, like 今; 金 means gold and metal.
金 (metal) — as a radical it shrinks to 钅 in simplified characters — 钱 money, 铁 iron, 钟 clock, 银 silver.

example.hanzi: 这条项链是纯黄金做的。
example.pinyin: zhè tiáo xiàngliàn shì chún huángjīn zuò de.
example.english: This necklace is made of pure gold.
example.fact: Gold is so malleable that a single ounce can be hammered into a sheet thin enough to cover 100 square feet, or drawn into a wire nearly 80 kilometers long. It's also one of the least reactive metals, which is why gold artifacts thousands of years old can still be found gleaming and untarnished. Almost all of the gold on Earth is thought to have arrived via asteroid impacts after the planet's crust had already formed.

examples.hanzi: 这块黄金很贵。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài huángjīn hěn guì.
examples.english: This piece of gold is very expensive.

examples.hanzi: 现在是学习汉语的黄金时间。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài shì xuéxí Hànyǔ de huángjīn shíjiān.
examples.english: Now is the golden time for studying Chinese.
